item.title: France's Philippe Diallo to challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency
item.description:
European football's governing body UEFA has given its "unanimous" backing to French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino in March's FIFA presidential election, it said in a statement Monday. Under its Slovenian president Aleksander Ceferin, UEFA has led the opposition to Infantino since his announcement in late July of a project to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes speaks with Dr. Emanuel Macedo de Medeiros, Co-founder and Global CEO of the Sport Integrity Global Alliance.

Covered by 3 public.
Sources: Al Jazeera English, Deutsche Welle, France 24

item.title: Macron visits Malaysia as France seeks closer defence and rare earths ties
item.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron will meet Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday to discuss strengthening defence, trade, energy and critical minerals co-operation. Macron's two-day visit, his first since 2017, comes ahead of the countries' 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations, with both sides seeking a strategic partnership.

Covered by 2 public.
Sources: Al Jazeera English, France 24

item.title: Ukraine: Russian strikes hit bridges in Kyiv, mayor says
item.description:
Russian strikes hit two major bridges in Kyiv late Monday, part of an overnight attack that damaged critical infrastructure and disrupted heating and water in parts of the capital, its mayor said. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky had warned of an attack by Russia in the coming days even as negotiators representing Kyiv as well as Europe and the United States held talks on future negotiations with Russia aimed at finding a path to end the war.

Covered by 2 public.
Sources: Deutsche Welle, France 24

item.title: Pope bids 'hasta luego' to Peru as he wraps up marathon South America trip
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV finished Monday his 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru reiterating his advocacy for social justice, environmental protection and the importance of community. Just a month after undergoing lung cancer surgery, the 71-year-old pontiff drew millions of faithful across South America, where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary.

Covered by 1 nonprofit, 1 public.
Sources: France 24, PBS NewsHour

item.title: New documentary explores history of crime and punishment in America
item.description:
A new four-episode PBS documentary series, Crime and Punishment in America , debuts tonight and offers a deeply researched and engaging history of the country's efforts to create a fair and humane justice system. Written, directed, and produced by Lynn Novick and executive produced by Ken Burns, the documentary explores one of the most interesting but lesser-explored angles of our country's history. Like Reason 's recent cover story on the history of American prisons, the documentary recognizes that the question of what criminal punishment in a constitutional republic should look like has been, outside of the problem of race, perhaps the country's most consequential and enduring debate over the last 250 years. item.title: Ukraine hits key Crimea bridge with drones
item.description:
Traffic temporarily restricted on key connection after bridge targeted during overnight drone barrage by Ukraine Ukraine has hit the Kerch bridge connecting occupied Crimea with Russia, in a symbolic blow that temporarily paralysed road traffic and left thousands of drivers stranded. A Ukrainian kamikaze drone crashed into one of the bridge’s arches at 5.38am local time, local channels reported.
